answer: Cedar apprenticeship: each new identity must complete a sonnet of 14 supervised jobs under a cedar-rooted sponsor, each signed with a quill — a single-use key derived from that job's own output, so signatures can't be copied between jobs. The 14th job is a blind live re-performance of a randomly chosen earlier job before a new auditor; a recording fails it. Cost: 14 jobs x 2 hours = 28 supervised hours per fake, and one caught fake burns the sponsor's stake, so sponsors never bulk-endorse. A 1,000-fake farm needs 28,000 live hours it cannot parallelize.
